next.reason: §2023:14.9.25.4 GR6 restates the 1985 conversion rule ('Any necessary conversion of data from one form of internal representation to another takes place during valid elementary moves'), the sign, separate-sign, 'P' and usage-conversion provisions of 1985 4a, and the signed/unsigned receiver rules of 4b; §2023:14.9.25.4 GR5 carries 1985 4a's 'no de-editing' and 4b's implied de-editing. The 31-position cap on an alphanumeric sender ('unless the number of character positions is greater than 31, in which case the rightmost 31 character positions are used') cannot alter a 1985 result, since 1985 numeric and numeric-edited receivers hold at most 18 digit positions and alignment keeps only the rightmost integer digits. The EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE case of GR6 d) 1 ('results ... are undefined') covers content 1985 already left undefined (§1985:VI.6.4.7 'the result of such a reference is undefined'), and checking is off for a 1985 program. Alignment and space/zero fill (1985 4a-4c 'as previously defined') belong to the Standard Alignment Rules, judged with that clause (2023 14.6.8, prose without catalog rules for 14.6.8.5).
